sections.label: International Arbitration Act history
sections.summary: The International Arbitration Act was introduced in 1994 and has been updated from time to time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our International Arbitration Act was introduced in 1994 and has been updated from time to time to be on the cutting-edge of international arbitration.

sections.label: Third-party funding agreements unenforceable
sections.summary: In Singapore, third-party funding agreements for dispute resolution proceedings are generally unenforceable under maintenance and champerty laws.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Currently, in Singapore, agreements for third-party funding of dispute resolution proceedings are generally unenforceable as they fall foul of the laws of maintenance and champerty.

sections.label: Bill abolishes champerty and maintenance
sections.summary: The Bill abolishes the tort of champerty and maintenance, permits third-party funding only for prescribed proceedings, starting with international arbitration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Bill clarifies that the common law tort of champerty and maintenance is abolished in Singapore, as had previously been stated by the High Court in Jane Rebecca Ong vs Lim Lie Hoa.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Third-party funding contracts will, therefore, still be unenforceable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: It is only for certain prescribed categories of proceedings that a third-party funding contract will not be contrary to public policy or illegal by reason that it is a contract for maintenance or champerty.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: At the outset, third-party funding will only be permitted for international arbitration proceedings and related Court and mediation proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This will allow the framework to be tested within a limited sphere by parties of commercial sophistication.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The framework may be broadened in future after a period of assessment.

sections.label: Lawyers must disclose third-party funding
sections.summary: The Legal Profession (Professional Conduct) Rules will be amended to require lawyers to disclose any third-party funding their client receives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition, the Legal Profession (Professional Conduct) Rules will be amended to impose a duty on lawyers to disclose the existence of any third-party funding which their client is receiving.

sections.label: Definition of third-party funding
sections.summary: Third-party funding is financing provided by financing firms for claims in arbitration or litigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Third-party funding is essentially financing provided by financing firms for claims in arbitration or litigation.

sections.label: Funders may take case control
sections.summary: Third-party funders may transfer control of cases from claimants and take control of strategy and decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One, third-party funders may transfer control of the cases from the claimants themselves and take control of the strategy and decision-making for cases which they fund.

sections.label: Third-party funding prolonged litigation
sections.summary: Third-party funding has resulted in prolonged litigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Three, third-party funding has resulted in prolonged litigation.

sections.label: Direct financial benefit definition
sections.summary: A question asks what "direct financial benefit" means under clause 3, proposed clause 3A(a) and clause 3B of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What is meant by the term "direct financial benefit" under clause 3 of the Bill where it proposed to include a clause 3A(a) and clause 3B?

sections.label: Bill abolishes maintenance and champerty
sections.summary: The Bill abolishes the tort of maintenance and champerty and carves out prescribed categories for funding contracts in arbitration and related proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill that is before this House is, therefore, crucial.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It abolishes the tort of maintenance and champerty; high time, some would say, given that the UK's abolition of the same came 50 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More importantly, the Bill boldly carves out "prescribed categories" regarding the enforceability of funding contracts for arbitration and arbitration-related proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These proceedings will not automatically be deemed as being contrary to public policy or illegal.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This amendment is important for Singapore to gain and maintain its competitive advantage over the other established and popular seats, namely, Geneva, New York, Stockholm and, most close to home, Hong Kong.

sections.label: Third-party funders' costs liability
sections.summary: A question asks what third-party funders' liability for costs will be, if any.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, on costs, what will the third-party funders' liability be for costs, if any?

sections.label: New funding option and safeguards
sections.summary: Parties can consider commercial choices, and safeguards include the Civil Law (Third-Party Funding) Regulations 2016 and lawyers engaged by funders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With this new option, parties to a dispute can now consider their commercial choices: how they might allocate risks, collateralise the claim or apply capital profitably, which may not otherwise have been available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, necessary to be alive to the need to retain the momentum as an arbitration hub, a status that Singapore has worked tirelessly to achieve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are a number of safeguards which will affect the funders, such as the Civil Law (Third-Party Funding) Regulations 2016, as well as the lawyers engaged by funders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It would be useful to consider if these current regulations sufficiently protect all stakeholders and whether they serve the intended purpose of permitting third-party funding.

sections.label: Bill amends Civil Law Act
sections.summary: The Civil Law (Amendment) Bill amends the Civil Law Act to abolish maintenance and champerty and allow third-party funding in certain proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to clarify if there is sufficient guidance on the effect of third-party funding on legal privilege and confidentiality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Civil Law (Amendment) Bill seeks to amend the Civil Law Act to abolish the common law tort of maintenance and champerty in Singapore and to allow third-party funders to provide funding in certain categories of dispute resolution proceedings, namely, international arbitration proceedings under the International Arbitration Act and related dispute resolution proceedings arising therefrom.

sections.label: Third-party funding in international arbitration
sections.summary: The proposed section 5B and regulations appear to allow third-party funding in Singapore only for international arbitration, at least for now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Yet, the proposed section 5B of the Bill, read with the proposed regulations, appears to allow only third-party funding in Singapore in the context of international arbitration, at least for now.

sections.label: Basis for limiting third-party funding
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State the basis for permitting third-party funding in international arbitration but not litigation and domestic arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: More fundamentally, if the objective of section 5A is to allow third-party funding contracts in the context of international arbitration only, I would like to ask the hon Senior Minister of State what is the basis for permitting third-party funding in the context of international arbitration but not litigation and domestic arbitration?

sections.label: Circumventing domestic arbitration funding restrictions
sections.summary: Parties to a domestic arbitration may agree to apply the International Arbitration Act, turning it international and circumventing proposed section 5B restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In respect of domestic arbitrations, I would like to highlight that the International Arbitration Act allows parties to a non-international arbitration to agree that the provisions of the International Arbitration Act would apply to the arbitration, thereby turning it to an international arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, parties to a domestic arbitration who wish to avail themselves of third-party funding may circumvent the proposed section 5B restrictions against third-party funding for domestic arbitrations in this manner.

sections.label: Allowing funding for litigation and domestic arbitration
sections.summary: The speaker urges reconsideration of limiting section 5A third-party funding to international arbitration, and to also allow it for litigation and domestic arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, third-party funding tends to filter out unmeritorious cases, because funders will not take on risks of such cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Therefore, if section 5A is intended to allow third-party funding only in the context of international arbitration, I urge a reconsideration of this position and to also allow third-party funding for litigation and domestic arbitration.

sections.label: Safeguards against third-party funding abuse
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry intends to impose further requirements to safeguard against potential abuse of third-party funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the 2011 consultation on the International Arbitration Act, the Ministry had proposed safeguards to third-party funding, to minimise potential abuse, such as restricting third-party funding by stipulating the permissible categories of practice areas, threshold claim value and minimum capital adequacy of third-party funders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In light of the potential risks of third-party funding, does the Ministry intend to impose further requirements so as to safeguard against the potential abuse of third-party funding?

sections.label: Regulation and supervision of third-party funders
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Senior Minister of State would consider regulation and supervision of third-party funders in Singapore by a Ministry, Statutory Board, Government body or self-regulatory body.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would the Senior Minister of State consider whether there should be some form of regulation and supervision over third-party funders in Singapore, whether by the Ministry, Statutory Board, Government body, or by a self-regulatory body, to ensure and enforce compliance with statutory qualifications and regulations?

sections.label: Third-party funding of litigation
sections.summary: The current legislation allows third parties to fund litigation expenses and appears focused on international arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In principle, this is what the current legislation is aiming to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It allows third parties to fund litigation expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It appears to be focused currently on international arbitration.

sections.label: Insurance analogy and contingency fees
sections.summary: The speaker calls the insurance analogy apposite, describes the arrangement as pooling of risks, and suggests future legislation consider contingency fee arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, there is a certain benefit in this certainly, and I think my colleague Mr Murali's analogy to insurance is actually quite apposite, because what this is really is a pooling of risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, if we are still taking access to justice as being one of the important aims for these more creative fee arrangements, I would suggest that future legislation go even further and consider looking into allowing contingency fee arrangements.

sections.label: Protecting vulnerable litigants
sections.summary: The speaker expects no US-style abuse of process but says consideration is needed on protecting vulnerable litigants from unfair fee arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, my guess is that we will probably not have the US-style abuse of process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I still think this is a move that requires some consideration, and certainly consideration needs to go into how we can protect vulnerable litigants, particularly in relation to fee arrangements that may be unfair to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By and large, if we are talking about ensuring access to justice, particularly for impecunious litigants, chances are that contingency fee arrangements are more likely to achieve that objective.

sections.label: Lawyer fees and impecunious litigants
sections.summary: A lawyer cannot peg fees to settlement proceeds, but this may be a workable solution for truly impecunious litigants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A lawyer cannot peg his fees to what you get from your settlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But the reality is that if you are talking about access to justice, this may be one of the workable solutions for the truly impecunious litigants.

sections.label: Abolishing maintenance and champerty
sections.summary: The speaker supports a Bill abolishing the common law tort of maintenance and champerty and allowing third-party funding contracts in prescribed categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If you are allowing a third-party to have an interest in the outcome of the litigation, there is no harm in allowing a lawyer to do that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think the abuses can be contained and the fundamental principle of access to justice will be enhanced if we allow these more creative fee arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The good news is that we are not pioneers in that area and we can definitely learn from all those who have gone before us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I rise to support this Bill which seeks to abolish the common law tort of maintenance and champerty in Singapore and allowing third-party funding contracts in certain prescribed categories of dispute resolution proceedings, as well as set out the regulations around this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: According to the SIAC Annual Report 2015, 84% of new cases filed with SIAC in 2015 were international in nature, and 42% had no connection with Singapore.

sections.label: Guidelines on third-party funding contracts
sections.summary: The passage states a first step is to promulgate a set of guidelines on entering into third-party funding contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, to promulgate a set of guidelines on entering into third-party funding contracts.

sections.label: Code of conduct for funders
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to promulgate a code of conduct for third-party funders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: My second suggestion is to promulgate a code of conduct for third-party funders.

sections.label: Third-party funding in arbitration
sections.summary: Third-party funding is first proceeding in the context of international arbitration and related proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As mentioned, we are first proceeding with third-party funding in the context of international arbitration and related proceedings.

sections.label: Contingency fee arrangements prohibited
sections.summary: Lawyers and law firms will continue to be prohibited from entering into contingency fee arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Until such time, lawyers and law firms will continue to be prohibited from entering into contingency fee arrangements.

sections.label: Proposed third-party funding framework
sections.summary: The proposed framework makes disclosure the central tenet while giving precedence to party autonomy and flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The proposed third-party funding framework, therefore, seeks to address these issues by making disclosure the central tenet, while giving precedence to party autonomy and flexibility.

sections.label: Prohibitions on practitioners and practices
sections.summary: Legal practitioners and practices are prohibited from holding shares or ownership interests in funders and from receiving referral fees and commissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Legal practitioners and legal practices will also be prohibited from holding any share or having ownership interests in relevant third-party funders and from receiving referral fees and commissions.

sections.label: Qualifying third-party funder criteria
sections.summary: Only entities meeting the qualifying third-party funder criteria may provide funding, and non-compliant entities cannot enforce their rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For completeness, I would highlight that the third-party funding framework will only allow entities which meet the "qualifying third-party funder" criteria to provide third-party funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The criteria will help to ensure that only reputable, professional funders may fund international arbitration proceedings in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Non-compliant entities will not be able to enforce their rights under the third-party funding agreement.

sections.label: Solicitor third-party funder referral
sections.summary: Subsection 3A allows a solicitor to introduce or refer a third-party funder to a client if the solicitor receives no direct financial benefit, which excludes client-paid legal fees, disbursements or expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Subsection 3A says that to avoid doubt, the section does not prevent a solicitor from introducing or referring a third-party funder to the solicitor's client, so long as the solicitor does not receive any direct financial benefit, and "direct financial benefit" is defined so that it does not include any fee, disbursement or expense payable by the solicitor's client for the provision of legal services by the solicitor to the client.

sections.label: Citation year change to 2017
sections.summary: The citation year "2016" will be changed to "2017", as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation year "2016" will be changed to "2017", as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
